description: Fig. 1 is a process schematic — a composite of roughly ten 3-D block diagrams (rectangular prisms) joined by thick black sequence arrows — that illustrates one multiaxial forging (MAF) cycle. The starting block, labelled "Original sample", is annotated 20 × 30 × 20 (mm) with a local x–y–z triad (x to the right, y up, z toward the viewer); a grey arrow labelled "1st compression" presses its top face. In the next block the pressed edge has shortened from 30 to 20 mm while a 20 mm edge has grown to 30 mm in the flow direction, the third (constrained) edge remaining 20 mm; later blocks carry the same 20/30 permutations. Rotation steps between blocks are labelled "90° Rotation about y axis", "90° Rotation About z axis" and "90° Rotation about x axis" (repeated around the loop). A central triad legend defines "Pressing direction", "Constrained direction" and "Flow direction". Three stages are titled "1st compression", "2nd compression" and "3rd compression"; the left-hand column terminates in a block labelled "Deformed sample". Flat orange, green and blue face colours track face identity through the rotations, not phases. No strain, stress or temperature numbers are printed; the only numerals are the 20 and 30 mm edge annotations.
measured_quantities: normal strain per pass (%, stated in citing text only)
equivalent strain per MAF pass (dimensionless, stated in citing text only)

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic of one MAF cycle built from about ten 3-D rectangular-prism blocks joined by thick black sequence arrows; it is not a micrograph, curve or spectrum.
The first block is labelled "Original sample" and is annotated with edge lengths 20, 30 and 20 (mm) plus a local x–y–z coordinate triad.
A grey arrow labelled "1st compression" presses the top face of the original sample; in the following block the pressed edge annotation has changed from 30 mm to 20 mm.

In the block after the 1st compression the three edge annotations are 20, 20 and 30 (mm), i.e. a 20 mm edge has expanded to 30 mm in the flow direction while the constrained edge stays 20 mm — consistent with constant-volume flow, but the figure prints no volume or strain value.
Rotation steps are printed between blocks as "90° Rotation about y axis", "90° Rotation About z axis" and "90° Rotation about x axis" (the x-axis label appears more than once along the loop).
Three blocks are titled by compression number: "1st compression", "2nd compression" and "3rd compression".
A central orthogonal triad legend names the three MAF directions as "Pressing direction", "Constrained direction" and "Flow direction", each drawn as a grey arrow.
The left-hand column of the diagram ends in a block labelled "Deformed sample".

Every block face is filled with a flat orange, green or blue colour and the colour pattern re-appears rotated in successive blocks, indicating the colours are face-tracking markers for the rotation steps rather than phase or constituent labels.
No strain, stress, temperature or time value is printed anywhere in the figure; the only numerals are the 20 and 30 mm edge annotations.
The caption states only that the figure is a schematic diagram of the MAF process and gives no dimensions or conditions.

The citing text states the workpiece is first compressed in a die to a fixed strain, then removed, rotated by 90 degrees about both the vertical and horizontal axes, and compressed again to the same strain.
The citing text states the initial sample height is decreased from 30 mm to 20 mm by a sequence of ram pressure, producing a 33% normal strain in a single pass.
The citing text states the equivalent strain in one-pass MAF is calculated to be 0.47; this number does not appear in the figure.

The citing text notes that because of the die constraint the blank deforms in height and expands in the flow direction but does not deform in the constrained direction, which matches the three annotated directions in the figure legend.

subfigures.description: Starting rectangular prism labelled "Original sample", annotated 20 (depth) × 30 (height) × 20 (width) mm, with an x–y–z coordinate triad and a grey downward arrow labelled "1st compression" on the top face. Orange top, green right and blue front faces.

Block whose annotated edge lengths are 20, 20 and 30 (mm): the pressed vertical edge is now 20 mm and a 30 mm edge lies in the in-plane flow direction. Followed by a black arrow labelled "90° Rotation about y axis".

Block drawn with the long 30 mm edge along the depth direction and 20 mm on the other two edges, i.e. the sample re-oriented by the 90° rotation; followed by an arrow labelled "90° Rotation About z axis".
Block titled "2nd compression" with a grey pressing arrow and annotations 20, 30, 20 (mm), showing the sample length again equal to 30 mm along one edge after the second pressing step.

Three mutually perpendicular grey arrows labelled "Pressing direction" (downward), "Constrained direction" (oblique) and "Flow direction" (horizontal), defining the deformation frame used for every block.
Block labelled "Deformed sample", annotated 20 × 30 × 20 (mm), closing the sequence at the left of the diagram.
Block under a large black downward arrow, titled "3rd compression", annotated with 20/20/30 (mm) edge lengths and x, y, z edge labels.

Chain of three further blocks linked by arrows labelled "90° Rotation about x axis", "90° Rotation about y axis" and "90° Rotation about z axis", returning to the "Deformed sample" block; each block repeats the 20/20/30 mm annotation with permuted axis labels.

unreadable_items: Exact axis assignment of the 20/30 mm annotations in the 2nd and 3rd compression blocks is ambiguous because of the 3-D perspective drawing
Which edge of the bottom-row blocks each "90° Rotation about ..." label applies to is not fully determinable at the supplied resolution
Some small x/y/z edge letters on the lower-right blocks are only partially readable
